specDocument:
## Rules

R1: The public method `String apply(String input)` must return a new `String` that reflects the stylistic transformation associated with the enum constant on which it is invoked.

R2: For the constant `UPPERCASE`, `apply` returns `input.toUpperCase()`.

R3: For the constant `LOWERCASE`, `apply` returns `input.toLowerCase()`.

R4: For the constant `CAPITALIZE_WORDS`, `apply` returns a string where each word (delimited by one or more whitespace characters) starts with an uppercase letter followed by only lowercase letters. Example: `"java programming"` → `"Java Programming"`.

R5: For the constant `REVERSE`, `apply` returns the characters of `input` in reverse order.

R6: The method `apply` requires a non‑null argument. Supplying `null` results in a `NullPointerException` being thrown.

## Worked Examples

| Rules | Input (style, string) | Expected |
|-------|-----------------------|----------|
| R2 | `UPPERCASE`, `"Hello World"` | `"HELLO WORLD"` |
| R4 | `CAPITALIZE_WORDS`, `"java programming language"` | `"Java Programming Language"` |
| R5 | `REVERSE`, `"abc"` | `"cba"` |

## Design

| Type | Role | Template status |
|------|------|-----------------|
| TextStyle | Enum that encapsulates four stylistic transformations; each constant implements `apply` with its own behaviour. | student-creates |
| TextProcessor | Utility class that delegates a call to `TextStyle.apply`. Provided fully so students have a concrete collaborator. | given |

## Public API

```java
public enum TextStyle {
    UPPERCASE,
    LOWERCASE,
    CAPITALIZE_WORDS,
    REVERSE;

    public abstract String apply(String input);
}
```

```java
public final class TextProcessor {
    public static String applyStyle(TextStyle style, String input) {
        return style.apply(input);
    }
}
```

## Testing Strategy

| ID | Owner type | Observable responsibility | Weight | After due date |
|----|------------|---------------------------|--------|----------------|
| S1 | TextStyle | `apply` returns the correct transformation for each enum constant. Partitions: uppercase, lowercase, capitalize‑words, reverse. | 3 | no |

## Contract Risk Inventory

| Seam | Rules | Admitted partitions | Excluded inputs |
|------|-------|---------------------|-----------------|
| S1 | R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6 | S1.P1: uppercase transformation; S1.P2: lowercase transformation; S1.P3: capitalize‑words transformation; S1.P4: reverse transformation | null (throws NPE) |

## Decision Ledger

| Decision | Provenance | Why necessary | Observable |
|----------|------------|----------------|------------|
| Enum name `TextStyle` and four constants | EXPLICIT_BRIEF | The brief asks for distinct text styles encapsulated in enum constants. | Enum type and constants exist. |
| Method `apply(String)` as the public entry point | EXPLICIT_BRIEF | Students must expose a callable behaviour per constant. | Public method signature present. |
| Null argument causes `NullPointerException` | NECESSARY_OPERATIONAL_CHOICE | Guarantees a well‑defined contract without requiring nullable handling inside student code. | R6 defined. |
| Definition of word boundaries for `CAPITALIZE_WORDS` as whitespace‑separated tokens | INPUT_DOMAIN_ASSUMPTION | Provides an unambiguous rule for capitalization. | R4 behavior deterministic. |
